summary: Bug hunt under his standing brief (#690): four areas, real touch/mouse input, every finding a failing test; one skeptic per finding; a fixer per area

confirmed.title: Letting go of a clip or trim edge he carried into the screen edge throws the timeline back, and what he just placed goes off screen
confirmed.see: On the phone he holds a clip and carries it to the right edge. The timeline scrolls with him, as #115 promised. The moment he lifts his finger the timeline jumps back to where the playhead was, and the clip he just placed ends up off the screen (x 629..755 on a 380 px screen). It happens the same way on PC with a trim handle: he drags a clip end into the edge, it extends while the view scrolls, and when he lets go the view jumps back about 1350 px. The new end is then at x 2615 on a 1280 px timeline. Either way he has to scroll to find what he just placed, which is exactly the chore #115 was built to save him.
confirmed.test: HUNT-a letting go of a clip or a trim edge he carried to the screen edge throws the timeline back — what he just placed goes off screen. Fails with: on the phone he held a clip and carried it to the right edge; the timeline scrolled with him (63 -> 383 px) and the clip sat under his finger at x 309..435; the moment he let go the timeline jumped back to 63 px and the clip is now at x 629..755, off a 380 px screen — he has to scroll to find what he just placed; AND on PC he dragged a clip end into the right edge and held it there; the timeline scrolled (174 -> 1521 px) and the new end sat under the pointer at x 1268; when he let go the timeline jumped back to 174 px and the end he just set is at x 2615, off a 1280 px timeline. Real touch at 380 in both passes. The real-mouse PC half runs only when the driver window is at least 1200 wide (the 1280 pass). Controls: trusted touch, the clip really moved or extended, the view really scrolled, and it was on screen at release.
confirmed.evidence: js/timeline.js:4416 — the scroll handler returns early while trimDrag/clipMove is live (`if (trimDrag || clipMove || kfDrag || scrub) return;`), so FM.time never follows the edge scroll that clipEdgeScroll (4224 `clipMove.startX -= moved`, 4250) and trimEdgeScroll perform. On release, js/timeline.js:4958-4959 (clip move) and 4981-4993 (trim) call autoFitDuration and then FM.timeline.rebuild() -> updatePlayhead. updatePlayhead then runs js/timeline.js:5250 `timelineEl.scrollLeft = targetScroll` with targetScroll = FM.time × px-per-second, which is the pre-drag time. That write is the snap-back.
confirmed.fix: On the release of a clipMove or trimDrag that auto-scrolled, adopt the time under the centre line: FM.scrubTime(snapT(scrollLeft / pxPerSec())), read at pointerup. Apply it AFTER autoFitDuration: scrubTime clamps to project.duration, and a trim does not grow the project until the fit runs. A temporary patch doing exactly this made both passes green; it was reverted.

verdict.reason:
This is a real bug he would hit. I re-ran the test in the worktree on port 8951 and it failed the same way twice. At the 1280 pass both halves failed with the same numbers the hunter reported. On the phone the view scrolled from 63 to 383 px, then jumped back to 63 px on release, which left the clip at x 629..755 on a 380 px screen. On PC with the trim handle it scrolled from 174 to 1521 px, jumped back to 174 px, and the new end was at x 2615. At the 380 pass the phone half failed the same way. The input was trusted CDP touch and mouse. The test's own checks confirm the clip really moved or extended, the view really scrolled, and the clip was on screen at the moment of release, so the fixture or synthetic input did not cause this. The worktree's js/timeline.js is identical to the main checkout's.

The code path agrees with the hunter. At js/timeline.js:4416 the scroll handler returns early while clipMove or trimDrag is live, so the scrolls that clipEdgeScroll and trimEdgeScroll write (lines 4217 and 4250) never move FM.time. On release, the clipMove branch (about 4958) and the trimDrag branch (about 4981-4993) both call FM.timeline.rebuild(). That runs updatePlayhead, and with the drag cleared its guard at 5249 lets line 5250 write scrollLeft = FM.time × pxPerSec. FM.time is still the time from before the drag, so the view snaps back.

Nothing in REQUESTS.md asks for this. #115 ('keep dragging a layer to the left or right without needing to let go and then scroll') is about not having to scroll by hand, and the snap-back forces exactly that scroll after release. The code's own fixed-centre rule (comment at 4396-4401) says the time under the centre line IS the current time, and it was written to fix the same kind of complaint he made ('I'm 40s in, click a clip, get sent to the start'). No comment or request says the view should jump back to the playhead after an edge-scroll. Anyone who drags a clip or trim end into the edge band will see it: the band is about 23 px on a 380 px phone.

confirmed.title: Reset speed (1x) leaves his animation behind: a fade at the end of a 2x clip now ends halfway through it
confirmed.see: He has a clip at 2x with an ordinary fade in and fade out. He taps ⋯ then Reset speed (1x). The clip doubles in length (1 s to 5 s), but its keyframes stay at 1, 1.5, 2.5 and 3 s. The fade-out now finishes at 3 s, so the clip is invisible for its whole second half (opacity 0 at 3.5 s), and any other animation on it runs at double speed against the footage. The Speed slider and the two speed-to-playhead buttons would have carried the keyframes along (#68: 'changing all the key frames automatically to slow or speed with the layer').
confirmed.test: HUNT-a Reset speed (1x) leaves his animation where it was — a fade at the end of a 2x clip now ends halfway through it. Fails with: his 2x clip faded in over its first half second and out over its last; after ⋯ then Reset speed (1x) the clip runs from 1 s to 5 s but its keyframes stayed at 1, 1.5, 2.5, 3 s — the fade-out now ends at 3 s and the clip is invisible for its whole second half (opacity 0.00 at 3.50 s); the Speed slider would have carried the fades to the new ends. Driven with real taps on the phone's ⋯ (#m-more) and on the menu item, in both passes. Control: speed really went to 1 and the length to 4 s.
confirmed.evidence: js/app.js:4840-4845, the 'Reset speed (1×)' item in FM.layerMenuItems: `layer.speed = 1; layer.duration = span;` then rebuild and commit. It never calls FM.scaleLayerKeyframes. Compare the Speed slider at js/inspector.js:5664 (`FM.scaleLayerKeyframes(layer, layer.duration / durBefore)`) and spdSolve at js/inspector.js:5611, which both scale keyframes. The item also skips the FM.refitGroupsFor (#626) and the source clamp that the slider does.
confirmed.fix: Record durBefore, set speed and duration, then call FM.scaleLayerKeyframes(layer, layer.duration / durBefore); the speed track is already excluded. Also call FM.refitGroupsFor(layer) and clamp to the source the way the slider does. A temporary one-line scaleLayerKeyframes patch made the test green; it was reverted.

confirmed.title: Trimming the head of a speed-ramped clip with its handle makes every kept frame jump
confirmed.see: He puts a speed ramp on a clip (0.5x rising to 2x) and drags its left handle 2 s in to cut the start. Every frame he kept jumps forward half a second of footage (15 frames): at 5 s the picture was source 3.625 s and becomes 4.125 s. It happens on the phone with a finger and on PC with the mouse. A flat-speed clip is fine. The A key and the phone's Trim-start button were fixed for exactly this in #914.2, but the handle he actually drags never was.
confirmed.test: HUNT-a trimming the head of a speed-ramped clip with its handle makes every kept frame jump. Fails with: on the phone he trimmed the head of a speed-ramped clip (0.5x rising to 2x) by dragging its left handle 2 s in: every frame he kept jumped — at 5 s the picture was source 3.625 s and is now 4.125 s, 0.50 s of footage skipped (15 frames), where the same drag on a flat 1.5x clip keeps its picture exactly; AND the same on PC. Real touch (hold 450 ms then drag) at 380 in both passes, and a real mouse at 1280 when the driver window is wide. Controls: the same gesture on a flat 1.5x clip keeps its picture within 0.01 s, and the head really moved to about 4 s.
confirmed.evidence: js/timeline.js:3904 and 3908, the head branch of applyTrimAt (the grip's drag): `const spL = ramped ? FM.speedAt(L, trimDrag.start + delta) : sp;` then `L.trimStart = trimDrag.trim + delta * spL`. That is the instantaneous rate at the new head times the whole cut. It should be the ramp integral FM.headSourceDelta, which FM.trimLayerHead (3988), clipTrimStart (96) and FM.extendClipTo (js/app.js:4537) all use. The existing tests 'speed ramps: trimming or extending an edge does not move the surviving picture' and 914.2 both drive FM.trimLayerHead and call it the grip's head trim, but the grip never calls it (the #912 audit made the same assumption). There is a related hole in the same function: the reversed right-edge branch uses sp = 1 for any ramp (js/timeline.js:3840, `extra = (nd - trimDrag.dur) * sp`), which FM.extendClipTo already fixed with speedAdvanceOver/speedAdvanceSolve.
confirmed.fix: Compute the source delta with FM.headSourceDelta on the layer as it was at the grab: put L.start/L.duration back to trimDrag.start/dur for the call, or add a helper that takes them. Re-solve the trimStart<0 clamp the way extendClipTo does, and send the reversed-tail branch through FM.speedAdvanceOver/speedAdvanceSolve. A temporary patch using headSourceDelta made both passes green; it was reverted.

I ran the test myself against the worktree on port 8951 and it failed at both widths with the same numbers the hunter gave: at 5 s the picture moved from source 3.625 s to 4.125 s. The flat 1.5x control held its picture, and the head really moved to about 4 s, so the gesture did trim and the test can tell right from wrong.

The code path confirms it. In js/timeline.js, the head branch of applyTrimAt (the code behind the grip's pointermove) sets trimStart to `trimDrag.trim + delta * spL`, where `spL = FM.speedAt(L, trimDrag.start + delta)`. That is the speed at the new head multiplied by the whole cut, not the ramp integral. Nothing corrects it on release: the pointerup handler only commits history and rebuilds.

The numbers match by hand. The ramp is 0.5 + 0.25·(t−2). Cutting 2 s to 4 s consumes 1.5 s of source by the integral, but the code writes 1.0 × 2 = 2.0 s. The difference is 0.5 s, about 15 frames.

The fixture is realistic:
- Speed keyframes are in absolute project time. That is how the inspector's speed keyframe button creates them (inspector.js:5549-5554) and what FM.speedAdvanceOver assumes.
- The input is a real CDP touch (held 450 ms) and a real CDP mouse on the visible left grip, checked with elementFromPoint.

The code comment at timeline.js:94 and the #912 audit finding (REQUESTS.md ~32487) both say the grip already asks before moving and keeps frames still. It does not, so nothing in REQUESTS.md makes this intended behaviour. The grip is the odd one out.

confirmed.title: Pressing Right to nudge a layer sideways puts a keyframe on its up-down animation and changes the move
confirmed.see: On PC, with a layer selected, he presses Right to nudge it 1 px. If the layer's Y is animated (an eased slide up, say), a new Y keyframe appears at the playhead and the slide he never touched changes shape. It is 125 px off where it was at 1.5 s and 2.5 s (1375 / 625 became 1250 / 750): the eased move is now a straight run into a new diamond followed by a shorter ease out of it. A layer sitting on a half pixel is also moved half a pixel on the axis he did not press, for the same reason.
confirmed.test: HUNT-a pressing Right to nudge a layer sideways puts a keyframe on its up-down animation and changes the move. Fails with: he pressed Right once to nudge a layer that slides up (Y keyframes at 1, 3 s, eased): it moved 1 px right, and a new Y keyframe appeared at the playhead (Y keyframes now at 1, 2, 3 s) — the slide he did not touch changed shape, 125 px off where it was at 1.5 / 2 / 2.5 s (1375, 1000, 625 became 1250, 1000, 750). Runs at 1280 in both passes, with a keydown dispatched on window (the handler does not depend on trusted input). Control: x really went 300 -> 301.
confirmed.evidence: js/app.js:8054-8055, the Arrow branch of the window keydown handler: `FM.setTransform(layer, 'x', Math.round(FM.evalProp(tr.x, FM.time) + dx), FM.time); FM.setTransform(layer, 'y', Math.round(FM.evalProp(tr.y, FM.time) + dy), FM.time);`. Both run on every arrow press, even when dy (or dx) is 0. FM.setTransform on an animated prop upserts a keyframe at the playhead (js/scene.js:335-344), and upsertKeyframe (js/scene.js:308) inserts it with e: 'linear', which takes over the easing of the segment it lands in.
confirmed.fix: Only write the axis that moved (`if (dx) …; if (dy) …;`). A temporary patch doing that made the test green; it was reverted. Whether a nudge on an animated axis should shift the whole animation like a canvas drag (FM.shiftTransform) instead of keyframing it is a separate direction question for him.

verdict.reason:
This is a real bug. I re-ran the test against the hunt4-a worktree on port 8951 and it failed with the numbers the hunter gave. One Right press moved x from 300 to 301, and it also put a new Y keyframe at the playhead (Y keys went from 1, 3 s to 1, 2, 3 s). The eased slide changed from 1375/1000/625 to 1250/1000/750 at 1.5/2/2.5 s. (Port 8951 was already being served from that same worktree, so my serve.sh call only failed with "address in use". The run was still against the right code.)

The cause is in js/app.js around lines 8054-8055, in the Arrow branch of the window keydown handler. It calls FM.setTransform on both x and y on every arrow press, even when dy (or dx) is 0. For an animated prop, setTransform (js/scene.js:335-344) always calls upsertKeyframe. That function (js/scene.js:308) pushes the new keyframe with e:'linear'. In this app a segment's easing belongs to the keyframe it ends on (evalProp resolves b.e, the end key), so the new linear key takes over the first half of the eased segment. The before/after numbers match that: a quadratic ease before, linear then ease after.

Why it is not a test artefact:
(1) The handler has no isTrusted check. Its only guards are inEdit, the overlay check and the selection. A real Right press with a layer selected on PC and focus not in a text field takes the same path, and the control confirmed the nudge ran (x went 300 to 301).
(2) The fixture is a state he can make in the app: two Y keyframes, with easeInOut on the end key. Easing on the end key is the app's own model.
(3) It is not behaviour he asked for. Nothing in REQUESTS.md asks for an arrow press to keyframe the axis he did not press. His stated rule for canvas moves is the opposite: a canvas drag uses FM.shiftTransform "never to add" a keyframe (js/canvas-edit.js:606-607). Writing an unmoved axis is a plain oversight.

Smaller side effect: Math.round on the unmoved axis also moves a static layer sitting on a half pixel by 0.5 px.

Severity medium is fair. It is PC-only, and a straight linear Y animation only gets an extra diamond with no visible change in shape. On any eased or custom-curve Y (or X, when he presses Up/Down), the move he did not touch changes shape, and the new diamond shows on the timeline.

The fix of writing only the axis that moved is correct. Whether a nudge on the moved axis should keyframe it or shift the whole animation like a drag is a separate question for Ezra.

verdict.reason:
This is a real bug that he would hit. I re-ran the test on port 8952 with the ?only=HUNT-b a tap in Free crop filter and got the same failure. A tap outside the box turned the 700x1200 crop into 16x16, and a tap 10 px in from the bottom-right corner changed it to 640x1135. The control step passed: a deliberate 30 px drag inside the box moved it, and Done wrote the result. So the tool was receiving the driver's trusted touch events, and the failure is not a routing artefact. The hunter's commit only adds tests; js/crop-tool.js is byte-identical to main.

Code path (js/crop-tool.js):
- onDown (line 92) starts a drag on every press. A press on a handle resizes, a press inside a partial box moves it, and any other press becomes mode 'new' (line 100).
- onMove (line 104) acts on the very first pointermove and has no slop.
- For 'new', line 115 sets rect.w/h = Math.max(MIN=16, |travel|). A 1 px tremble therefore becomes a 16x16 box at the fingertip.
- For a handle, lines 118-121 set the edge to the finger's position rather than the edge plus the finger's travel. With a 16 px hit radius (line 84), the corner jumps up to 16 CSS px to the finger. This happens on any tap, and at the start of every real handle drag too.

- The fixture is ordinary: a 1080x1920 photo layer with a plain-number crop box, the same shape commit() writes.
